shared_elements: horizontal band of repeated motifs (zigzag band in A, rosette band in B)
circular/disc-like motifs (rounded forms in A, rosettes in B)
registers separating an upper figural zone from a patterned strip
justification: Both are shallow relief carvings on pale stone that divide the surface into a figural zone and a horizontal band of small repeated units (a zigzag/chevron strip in A, a row of rosettes in B), and both include an anthropomorphic figure among other carved forms. Beyond that generic scheme they diverge sharply: A is a coarse, rounded, sculpturally lumpy pillar dominated by animals set irregularly on a monolith, while B is a crisp, flat, geometrically controlled wall relief with finely ruled drapery folds and precisely repeated ornament set into fitted masonry blocks.
